tool.name: structured_query
tool.description:
Resolve a path in a YAML or JSON file to its value and exact 1-based line range.
Use this to find the precise file:line for a finding in a workflow, IaC, or config file (.yml/.yaml/.json) so you can cite it in code_locations — instead of reporting it without a location. When a vulnerability lives in a config structure (a GitHub Actions step's run: block, a permissions: stanza, a JSON policy element), DO NOT guess the line by eyeballing read_file output: call structured_query with the structural path and use the returned start_line/end_line directly.
This is the structured-file companion to code_graph (which covers Go/TS source). For raw HCL (.tf), this tool does NOT apply — only .tf.json is JSON.
tool.details: Backed by PyYAML node marks (YAML) and a JSON offset scanner (stdlib). Multi-line block scalars like 'run: |' return the full span (start_line..end_line covering every line of the block). Returns the parsed value, the start_line/end_line, and the raw snippet text.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Relative path to a .yml/.yaml/.json file in the repo. No leading slash, no '..' traversal. Example: ".github/workflows/rw-security.yml"

parameter.name: path
parameter.description: Structural path into the document. Dotted keys plus [n] indices: - "permissions" — a top-level key/block - "jobs.build.steps[3].run" — the run block of the 4th step of the build job - "rules[0].http[1].match" — nested arrays Keys containing '.' or '[' are not expressible this way; use structured_find for those.

returns.description: On success: file, path, start_line, end_line (1-based, inclusive; block scalars span all their lines), value (parsed), snippet (raw text). On failure: error (path not found, malformed path, unsupported file type, unreadable file).

tool.examples:
# Locating a GitHub Actions injection sink for code_locations
.github/workflows/ci.yml jobs.build.steps[2].run
# Finding the line range of an over-broad permissions block
.github/workflows/deploy.yml permissions
# A JSON IAM policy statement
policy.json Statement[0].Action

tool.name: structured_find
tool.description:
Find every mapping/object KEY in a YAML or JSON file whose name matches a regex, with each match's path and line range.
Use for "where is X configured" or "how many places set Y" across a config file — e.g. find every permissions: block, every run: step, or every key named *_token. Returns up to 50 matches. Pair with structured_query when you need the value at a specific match.
tool.details: Walks mapping keys (YAML) / object keys (JSON) recursively and regex-matches each key name. Returns path + start_line/end_line per hit. Does not match values — only keys.

parameter.name: file
parameter.description: Relative path to a .yml/.yaml/.json file. No leading slash, no '..'.

parameter.name: key_regex
parameter.description: Python regex matched against each key name (re.search semantics). Examples: "^run$" (exact), "token|secret|password" (any), "^permissions$".

returns.description: On success: file, matches (list of {path, start_line, end_line}), output (human-readable summary). When no keys match: output noting zero matches.

tool.examples:
# Where is permissions set across this workflow?
.github/workflows/rw-security.yml ^permissions$
# Every run: step (candidate injection sinks)
.github/workflows/ci.yml ^run$
